subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB358 LANDED 2026-09-09. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 'If the KEY phrase is not specified, the behavior is the same as if KEY IS EQUAL TO data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 had been specified' -> OK, GR15): '... with data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 being the prime record key for the file.'
WHY CONFORMS RATHER THAN PARTIAL, and it is the verdict question this row was held open on. GR15's SUBJECT is the START statement's omitted-KEY-phrase behaviour, a facility this implementation CLAIMS; record-key-name-1 appears only as the SECOND SPELLING of 'the prime record key'. That spelling is declined, not missing: Annex A.3 item 40 makes the SOURCE phrase that declares it processor-dependent, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40 records the decline, and COBOL1954 now REFUSES it BY NAME at every edition on both clauses (the sibling row SR-14.9.41.3-7 owns that half and carries DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT). The discriminator is the owner's own, set on SR-12.4.5.9.3-1 (kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02): a rule whose subject is a claimed facility conforms once the declined operand class is refused by name and witnessed; PARTIAL would say the implementation is incomplete, which after this landing it is not - the operand class is unwritable BY DECISION and the decision is diagnosed.
CODE: with st.startKeyPhrase() null, BindStart takes op '==' and, on the indexed arm, keyIndex -1 (the prime key) with operand file.RecordKeyItem - which is exactly 'as if KEY IS EQUAL TO data-name-1 had been specified, with data-name-1 being the prime record key'.
THE TEST THIS ROW WAS MISSING NOW EXISTS. The previous note recorded 'No spec-derived test covers the omitted-KEY form (both conformance goldens that use START write KEY IS >=) - test-needed'; conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb358_start_no_key_phrase closes it, and its discriminating leg is L2, not L1. An implementation that implied '>=' for the omitted KEY phrase passes an equality probe unchanged, because the record whose key EQUALS the operand is also the first whose key is >= it. L2 gives the prime key a value strictly BETWEEN two records ('AB99' over AB01/AB02/CD03), where the implied EQUAL finds no record and 14.9.41.4 GR17 e) 2 raises the invalid key condition (I-O status '23' - derived, not assumed: 9.1.13.5's other invalid-key values '21', '22' and '24' can only arise from a WRITE or REWRITE, so 9.1.13.1's tie-break is never reached), while an implied '>=' would SUCCEED and position at CD03. L3 is the complement: the same operand value under an explicit KEY IS >= succeeds and reads CD03, so L2's '23' cannot be read as the file, the operand or the verb being broken. MEASURED: the run matched the spec-derived .out line for line on its first execution.
EDITIONS: GR15 carries no edition marker and Annex E lists no 14.9.41 change, so the data-name-1 spelling is live at all four; the golden runs at --std 85, the oldest, where a mis-gated construct would show first. kb/Work PB1099 Q1 (w1095i): the record-key SOURCE phrase is PROVIDED (owner rule R65); the record-key-name-1 spelling: START with no KEY phrase on a SOURCE-form prime key is EQUAL on the concatenation (golden line F1). retired-witness: conformance:cases/12.4.5.6-ALTERNATE-RECORD-KEY/pb358-alternate-key-source (the COBOL1954 decline of the SOURCE phrase is retired: kb/Work PB1099 provides it) retired-witness: conformance:cases/12.4.5.6-ALTERNATE-RECORD-KEY/pb358-record-key-source (the COBOL1954 decline of the SOURCE phrase is retired: kb/Work PB1099 provides it)
